messages.subject: Re: Meta analysis
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rodrigo,

It depends on the nature of the experiments, the aim of the meta-
analysis, and how much you are willing to much about.

In general, R/qtl is written to deal with a single backcross or
intercross.  But you can use the c.cross function to combine crosses
(provided that their genetic maps are in line), and you can do the
linkage analysis with "cross" as a covariate.  But it won't be too
easy to do this properly.

regards,
karl

messages.subject: permutations
messages.body_plain:
Hello:

How does scanone.perm work? Does it permute phenotypes across all
individuals on a constant set of genotypes?  Also, the output of
scanone.perm is a vector length n consisting of the max LOD for each
of n permutations, correct?  Is there an easy way to retrieve the
genome scan results for permutations, i.e. LOD score at each maker for
each permutation?

Thanks so much for your help.

Charles

messages.subject: Re: permutations
messages.body_plain:
Dear Charles,

Yes, phenotypes are permuted across all individuals; phenotypes and
genotypes are fixed, and the associations among genotypes is preserved.

And yes, the output of scanone.perm gives the genome-wide maximum LOD
score for each permutation replicate.

If you want the genome scan results for each position at each
replicate, you'd need to code it up yourself, as in the following:

    data(hyper)
    hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)

    operm <- NULL
    n.perm <- 100
    n.ind <- nind(hyper)
    temp <- hyper

    for(i in 1:n.perm) {
      temp$pheno <- temp$pheno[sample(nind(temp)),]
      tempout <- scanone(temp)
      operm <- rbind(operm, tempout[,3])
    }

The operm object would then have one row per replicate, with columns
being the LOD scores at a grid across the genome.

karl

messages.subject: Rqtl on Mac computer
messages.body_plain:
This may well be a ridiculous posting, but I'm getting a bit
frustrated.  Normally I use PC, but I'm trying to run Rqtl on a Mac
system (OS 10.3.9) and I'm actually stumped at how to get it to
recognize my data.  I made the working directory "/Applications/R
workfiles" and yet the system refuses to read in my cross data.  I
assume there's some kind of ridiculous problem with my read.cross
statement, but I'm not at all familiar with Mac and so I have no idea
what it doesn't like about the statement.  The statement is as the
following:

f2sex.f2 <- read.cross(format="csvs",dir="MEB-USC/Applications/R
workfiles",genfile="F235x51o_gpe.csv",phefile="F235x51o_phe.csv",na.strings="NA",genotypes=c("A","H","B"))

However, this produces the following message:

Error in file(file, "r") : unable to open connection
In addition :  Warning message :
cannot open file 'MEB-USC/Applications/R workfiles/F235x51o_gpe.csv',
reason 'No such file or directory'

I don't suppose any Mac Rqtl users out there have a quick and easy
answer to what I'm doing wrong?  The first message makes me suspect
there's a problem in R itself or somethng.
